name: VoronoiCells
description: The plane divided by which scattered point is nearest, with the sites drifting so every border moves with them

notes: Nine cells is the whole search. Each site is jittered inside its own lattice cell and capped so it can never leave, so the nearest site to a pixel is in that pixel cell or one of the eight around it: nine hashes and nine distances, no list, no sorting and no texture.

The borders come from the second nearest site. Halfway between two sites the two distances are equal, so their difference goes to zero at the boundary, which is a usable distance to the edge for nothing. It is slightly wrong where three cells meet, by an amount nobody has noticed.
The wobble radius is capped just under a half. A site that crosses into its neighbour cell breaks the assumption the three by three search rests on, and the field tears along the lattice.
Nine hashes, nine distances and a smoothstep per pixel, with no loop over anything but the fixed three by three. Measured with pnpm gputime, which asks the GPU rather than timing the draw call.

near.description: Cell colour at the near end of the ramp.

mid.description: Cell colour through the middle. Between two colours a ramp gives one hue and a tint of it; passing through a third is what makes a field of flat cells read as lit from somewhere.

far.description: Cell colour at the far end.

edge.description: The borders between cells. Near-black with a little of the cell hue still in it, because a true black line across a saturated cell reads as a gap rather than as an edge.

cells.description: Cells across the short edge. Few and large reads as stained glass; past about twenty the borders are closer together than the cells are wide and it becomes a texture.

wobble.description: How far each site drifts from the middle of its own cell, in cell widths. Capped just under a half on purpose: a site that crosses into its neighbour cell breaks the nine-cell search and the field tears along the lattice. At 0 nothing moves, which costs nothing to draw and is a legitimate way to use it.

thickness.description: Border width, in lattice units. At 0 there are no borders and the cells are held apart by colour alone, which is quieter and entirely usable.

softness.description: Softness of the border, on top of the one pixel of antialiasing that is always there. A little helps more here than on a straight line, because a Voronoi border meets its neighbours at angles that are never the same twice.

depth.description: How much a cell darkens away from its own site. Just enough that a large cell does not read as a flat sticker; past about 0.4 it is a gradient competing with the borders for attention.

seed.description: Where every site sits and which cell takes which colour. Every value is a different field and none is better than another.

period.description: Seconds for one circuit of the sites. The loop closes exactly on it, because each site completes a whole turn of its own small circle in that time.

instruction: the sites drift and every border moves with them

credit.what: The parameter set and the pair of colours. Their Voronoi names two cell colours, a border, a scale, a seed and an edge intensity and softness, which is the right set, and the blue and magenta are theirs: far enough apart in hue to separate every cell from its neighbours without either reading as a highlight. The tessellation is Georgy Voronoy from 1908. The code here is this repo own.
credit.author: Shader Effects Inc.
